newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to hold events on racial harmony.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to hold events on racial harmony.

text.p: President Clinton will hold a series of events around the country focusing on easing racial tensions and will name an advisory council on improving race relations, White House officials said Thursday.

Clinton, who will use a speech in California next week to focus on racial harmony, intends to conduct a series of town hall meetings around the country to discuss the issue, spokesman Joe Lockhart said.
White House officials also said Clinton was expected to appoint an advisory panel to work with him on improving race relations throughout the country.

Presidential advisers have been meeting for several months discussing possible steps Clinton could take to promote racial harmony -- a goal he stressed when he took the oath of office for a second term in January.

On Wednesday Clinton met for about one hour with civil rights leader Jesse Jackson and Wade Henderson, executive director of the Civil Rights Leadership Conference, and discussed the June 14 address the president will deliver at the University of California at San Diego.
